questions.question: Distinguish between traditional and symbolic logic / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Tradiitonal logic: Based on Aristotelean logic
  • Uses ordinary language
  • Unit of analysis is terms
  • Limited to simple forms of reasoning
  • Symbolic logic: Based on modern mathematical logic
  • Uses symbols
  • Unit of analysis is proposition
  • Involves simple and complex reasoning

questions.question: Write a short note on statement form with examples / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Simple proposition: Expresses a single idea
  • Contains one variable
  • Eg.p , q
  • Complex proposition: Combines 2 or more simple propositions
  • Contains more than one variable which are connected with \
  • logical connectives
  • Eg. p.q, pv r etc

questions.question: Symbolise the following in predicate logic a. Radha is intelligent b. New Delhi is the capital of India c. Ravi is an engineer d. Govind is intelligent and hardworking e. Columbus is a traveller / [CO4] [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
Step-by-Step Valuation Scheme:
1. Theoretical Framework & Assumptions (2.0 Marks): Statement of foundational premises, variables, and starting conditions.
2. Analytical Development & Proof Steps (2.0 Marks): Rigorous derivation, systematic reasoning, and logical progression.
3. Synthesized Conclusion & Interpretation (2.0 Marks): Final formulated result, physical/academic significance, and domain limitations.
Model Solution: Provide structured answers with numbered points or labeled steps. Ensure all intermediate calculations or logical assertions are fully supported with standard university academic rigor.

questions.question: Critically examine the limitations of propositional logic and explain how predicate logic overcomes them. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Propositional logic:
  • • Treats whole proposition as single unit.
  • • Lacks Internal analysis.
  • • Statements involving generality cannot be expressed
  • Predicate logic
  • • Internal analysis is possible
  • • Uses quantifiers to express generality
  • • Relationship between terms are expressed
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss how constants and variables are used in propositional logic and predicate logic. Illustrate / [CO2]
questions.solution_html: • In propositional logic: Constants represent whole propositions Denoted by capital letters Eg P Q Variables represent unspecified propositions It is rarely used In predicate logic Constants represent specific individuals or objects Eg, R, S Variables represent arbitrary objects Eg. x, y

questions.question: Discuss how categorical propositions are analysed in predicate calculus / [CO4] [12x2 = 24]
questions.solution_html:
• Four types of categorical propositions
  • A- Universal affirmative represented as (x)(Sx→Px)
  • E- Universal negative - (x)(Sx→~Px)
  • I.Particular affirmative- (Ǝx) (Sx. Px)
  • O- Particular negative- (Ǝx)( Sx. ~Px)
